question: The term 'Butterfly stroke' is associated with which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swimming.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The butterfly stroke is one of the four competitive strokes in swimming. (तितली शैली — तैराकी)

 

• The four recognised strokes are:
◦ Freestyle (front crawl) — the fastest
◦ Backstroke — the only stroke started in the water
◦ Breaststroke — the slowest
◦ Butterfly — the most physically demanding, in which both arms move together over the water with a simultaneous dolphin kick

 

• In the individual medley the order of strokes is butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke and freestyle; in the medley relay it is backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly and freestyle.

 

• Other swimming terms: lap, lane, false start, flip turn, medley, freestyle and dolphin kick.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Swimming is governed by World Aquatics (formerly FINA). An Olympic-size pool is 50 metres long with 8 or 10 lanes.

 

• Indian swimmers of note: Sajan Prakash, the first Indian swimmer to qualify for the Olympics by the "A" standard; Srihari Nataraj; and Bula Choudhury and Arati Saha, who swam the English Channel — Arati Saha being the first Asian woman to do so, in 1959.

 

• Terms of other sports: Boxing — jab, hook, uppercut, knockout; Gymnastics — vault, beam, pommel horse, somersault; Table Tennis — smash, chop, loop, deuce, let.

 

NOTE

 

• Boxing (Option 2): Uses terms such as jab, hook and knockout.

 

• Gymnastics (Option 3): Uses vault, beam and pommel horse.

 

• Table Tennis (Option 4): Uses smash, chop, loop and deuce.

question: The Golconda Fort is located in which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Telangana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Golconda Fort is situated near Hyderabad in Telangana. It was originally a mud fort of the Kakatiyas, and was rebuilt in granite by the Qutb Shahi rulers, who made it their capital before founding Hyderabad. (गोलकुंडा किला — तेलंगाना)

 

• The fort is famous for its acoustics — a clap at the Fateh Darwaza, the entrance gate, can be heard clearly at the Bala Hisar pavilion nearly a kilometre away at the top of the hill, a device used to warn of danger.

 

• Golconda was for centuries the centre of the diamond trade, and the Kohinoor, the Hope Diamond and the Darya-i-Noor are all said to have passed through its markets. The Qutb Shahi tombs stand close by.

 

• The fort was captured by Aurangzeb in 1687, after a siege of eight months, which ended the Qutb Shahi dynasty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Important forts of India and their states:
◦ Gwalior Fort — Madhya Pradesh; called the "Gibraltar of India" by Babur
◦ Sinhagad, Raigad, Pratapgad, Shivneri, Daulatabad — Maharashtra
◦ Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Amber, Jaisalmer, Ranthambore, Gagron, Jaigarh — Rajasthan; six of these form the Hill Forts of Rajasthan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site
◦ Red Fort and Purana Qila — Delhi
◦ Agra Fort — Uttar Pradesh
◦ Fort St. George — Chennai; Fort William — Kolkata
◦ Bekal Fort — Kerala; Warangal Fort — Telangana

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Site of the Gwalior Fort and the Mandu complex.

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Site of the Gol Gumbaz at Vijayapura and the Chitradurga Fort.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Site of the great Maratha forts, including Raigad and Sinhagad.

question: The Raisina Dialogue, India's flagship annual conference on geopolitics and geo-economics, is organised by the Ministry of External Affairs in partnership with which institution?
option_2: Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses
solution_text:
The correct answer is Observer Research Foundation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Raisina Dialogue is organised by the Ministry of External Affairs in partnership with the Observer Research Foundation (ORF), a New Delhi think tank. (रायसीना संवाद — विदेश मंत्रालय एवं ओआरएफ)

 

• It was begun in 2016 and is held annually at New Delhi. It is India's flagship conference on geopolitics and geo-economics, and is modelled on the Shangri-La Dialogue of Singapore and the Munich Security Conference.

 

• It takes its name from Raisina Hill, the seat of the Government of India, on which stand the Rashtrapati Bhavan and the Central Secretariat.

 

• The conference brings together heads of state and government, ministers, military commanders, business leaders, scholars and journalists, and each edition is organised around a stated theme.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major dialogues and summits associated with India: the Delhi Dialogue (with ASEAN), the Indian Ocean Conference, the Vibrant Gujarat Global Summit and the World Sustainable Development Summit organised by TERI.

 

• India hosted the G20 Summit at New Delhi in September 2023, under the theme "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — One Earth, One Family, One Future", at which the African Union was admitted as a permanent member of the G20.

 

NOTE

 

• Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses (Option 2): Now the Manohar Parrikar IDSA, a defence think tank funded by the Ministry of Defence.

 

• Indian Council of World Affairs (Option 3): Established in 1943 and housed at Sapru House, New Delhi; it organises other conferences but not the Raisina Dialogue.

 

• Centre for Policy Research (Option 4): A public policy think tank at New Delhi, not associated with this conference.

question: The Khelo India Youth Games were held for the first time in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2018.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Khelo India Youth Games were held for the first time in 2018 at New Delhi, where they were then called the Khelo India School Games. (खेलो इंडिया यूथ गेम्स — 2018)

 

• The Khelo India programme was launched in 2017-18 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to revive the sports culture of the country at the grassroots level, by building a strong framework for all sports and establishing India as a great sporting nation.

 

• Selected athletes receive an annual scholarship of ₹5 lakh for eight years, covering training, competition, equipment and boarding.

 

• The programme now includes the Khelo India Youth Games, the Khelo India University Games (first held at Bhubaneswar in 2020), the Khelo India Winter Games (held at Gulmarg and Leh) and the Khelo India Para Games (first held in 2023).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major sports initiatives: the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS), launched in 2014 to support elite athletes; the Fit India Movement, launched on 29 August 2019; and the National Sports Development Fund.

 

• 29 August, the birth anniversary of Major Dhyan Chand, is observed as National Sports Day, on which the national sports awards are conferred.

 

• India's best performance at the Olympics came at Paris 2024, and at the Asian Games 2022 (held in 2023) at Hangzhou India won a record 107 medals.

 

NOTE

 

• 2016 (Option 1): The year of the Rio Olympics and of the first Raisina Dialogue, but not of the Khelo India Games.

 

• 2020 (Option 3): The year of the first Khelo India University Games, at Bhubaneswar.

 

• 2022 (Option 4): The year in which India won the Thomas Cup for the first time.

question: Which of the following ancient cities was the capital of the Kuru Mahajanapada?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indraprastha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indraprastha was the capital of the Kuru Mahajanapada, and is identified with a site in present-day Delhi, near the Purana Qila. (इंद्रप्रस्थ — कुरु महाजनपद की राजधानी)

 

• In the Mahabharata, Indraprastha is described as the capital built by the Pandavas in the Khandava forest. Hastinapura, on the Ganga in present-day Meerut district, was the capital of the Kauravas and the older seat of the Kuru clan.

 

• The sixteen Mahajanapadas of the sixth century BCE are listed in the Buddhist Anguttara Nikaya and the Jaina Bhagavati Sutra. Important capitals:
◦ Magadha — Rajgir (Girivraja), later Pataliputra
◦ Kosala — Shravasti; Kashi — Varanasi; Anga — Champa
◦ Vajji — Vaishali; Malla — Kusinara and Pava
◦ Vatsa — Kaushambi; Chedi — Sotthivati
◦ Kuru — Indraprastha; Panchala — Ahichhatra and Kampilya
◦ Matsya — Viratnagar; Surasena — Mathura
◦ Avanti — Ujjayini and Mahishmati; Assaka — Potali
◦ Gandhara — Taxila; Kamboja — Rajapura

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Of the sixteen, four grew powerful — Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa and Avanti — and Magadha eventually absorbed them all.

 

• The seven historical cities of Delhi are traditionally listed as Lal Kot/Qila Rai Pithora, Siri, Tughlaqabad, Jahanpanah, Firozabad, Din Panah (Purana Qila) and Shahjahanabad.

 

NOTE

 

• Kaushambi (Option 1): The capital of Vatsa, whose famous ruler was Udayana.

 

• Ahichhatra (Option 3): The capital of northern Panchala; southern Panchala had its capital at Kampilya.

 

• Mathura (Option 4): The capital of the Surasena Mahajanapada, and later an important centre of the Kushana empire and of a distinctive school of sculpture.

question: The headquarters of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is located in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lausanne.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Olympic Committee (IOC) has its headquarters at Lausanne, Switzerland, which is for that reason known as the "Olympic Capital". (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय ओलंपिक समिति — लुसाने, स्विट्ज़रलैंड)

 

• The IOC was founded on 23 June 1894 at Paris by Baron Pierre de Coubertin, who is called the Father of the Modern Olympics. 23 June is observed every year as Olympic Day.

 

• The first modern Olympic Games were held at Athens in 1896. The Olympic motto was "Citius, Altius, Fortius" — Faster, Higher, Stronger — to which "Communiter" (Together) was added in 2021. The five interlocking rings represent the five inhabited continents.

 

• The Olympic Museum is also at Lausanne, and the Court of Arbitration for Sport has its seat there.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Headquarters of major sports and international bodies:
◦ FIFA — Zurich, Switzerland
◦ ICC — Dubai, UAE
◦ FIH (hockey) and FIDE (chess) — Lausanne, Switzerland
◦ BWF (badminton) — Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
◦ World Athletics — Monaco
◦ WADA — Montreal, Canada
◦ WHO, ILO, WTO and the Red Cross — Geneva
◦ UNESCO and the OECD — Paris

 

• The First World Conference on Doping in Sport was convened by the IOC at Lausanne in February 1999, and led to the creation of WADA later that year.

 

NOTE

 

• Geneva (Option 2): Headquarters of the WHO, ILO and WTO, but not of the IOC. Both cities are in Switzerland, which makes this the commonest confusion in the question.

 

• Paris (Option 3): The city where the IOC was founded in 1894, and the host of the 2024 Olympic Games, but not its headquarters.

 

• Montreal (Option 4): Headquarters of WADA, the World Anti-Doping Agency.

question: Which of the following is the purest naturally occurring form of carbon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Diamond.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Diamond is the purest naturally occurring form of carbon, consisting of carbon atoms alone in a rigid three-dimensional network. (हीरा — कार्बन का शुद्धतम प्राकृतिक रूप)

 

• In diamond each carbon atom is bonded to four others in a tetrahedral arrangement, which makes it the hardest natural substance known. It is a bad conductor of electricity, because no free electrons are available, but an excellent conductor of heat.

 

• In graphite, by contrast, each carbon atom is bonded to only three others, forming hexagonal layers held together by weak forces. The layers slide over one another, which makes graphite soft and slippery and useful as a lubricant and in pencils; the fourth electron is free, so graphite conducts electricity.

 

• Diamond and graphite are allotropes — different physical forms of the same element. Fullerene (C-60, buckminsterfullerene) is a third allotrope, and carbon nanotubes and graphene are others.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Coke is an almost pure form of carbon obtained by the destructive distillation of coal, and is used as a reducing agent in metallurgy.

 

• Other impure forms of carbon: charcoal (from wood), lampblack, carbon black and coal.

 

• Carbon is called the "king of the elements" because of catenation — its unique ability to link with itself in long chains and rings, which gives rise to the whole of organic chemistry. Carbon-14 is used in radiocarbon dating.

 

NOTE

 

• Coal (Option 1): A fossil fuel containing carbon along with hydrogen, sulphur, nitrogen and mineral matter; far from pure.

 

• Graphite (Option 2): A pure crystalline allotrope, but softer and structurally quite different; it is not regarded as the purest form.

 

• Charcoal (Option 3): An amorphous and impure form of carbon obtained by heating wood in the absence of air.

question: Who was the first Indian to be awarded the Nobel Prize?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian — and the first Asian — to be awarded the Nobel Prize, receiving the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for "Gitanjali" (Song Offerings). (रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर — प्रथम भारतीय नोबेल पुरस्कार विजेता, 1913)

 

• He composed "Jana Gana Mana", the national anthem of India, and "Amar Sonar Bangla", the national anthem of Bangladesh. He founded Visva-Bharati at Santiniketan in 1921, and renounced his knighthood in 1919 in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

 

• Indian and Indian-origin Nobel laureates:
◦ Rabindranath Tagore — Literature, 1913
◦ C.V. Raman — Physics, 1930, for the Raman Effect; the first Indian in the sciences
◦ Har Gobind Khorana — Medicine, 1968 (Indian-born, US citizen)
◦ Mother Teresa — Peace, 1979
◦ Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar — Physics, 1983 (Indian-born, US citizen)
◦ Amartya Sen — Economics, 1998
◦ Venkatraman Ramakrishnan — Chemistry, 2009
◦ Kailash Satyarthi — Peace, 2014, shared with Malala Yousafzai
◦ Abhijit Banerjee — Economics, 2019

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nobel Prizes were instituted under the will of Alfred Nobel, the Swedish inventor of dynamite, and were first awarded in 1901. They are conferred on 10 December, the anniversary of his death.

 

• The Prize in Economic Sciences was instituted in 1968 by the Sveriges Riksbank, and is not one of the original five.

 

• Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, and the first person to win it twice — in Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911).

 

NOTE

 

• C.V. Raman (Option 2): The first Indian to win a Nobel Prize in the sciences, in 1930, but seventeen years after Tagore.

 

• Mother Teresa (Option 3): Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979.

 

• Har Gobind Khorana (Option 4): Awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1968; born at Raipur in undivided Punjab, he was by then a citizen of the United States.
